assessment.where_you_stand: As an employee who has resigned, you have a strong legal right to receive your full and final settlement. Under the law, when an employee resigns, wages due must be paid within two working days [KB:src_cow_2019_17], making the company's 90-day policy legally questionable. Your strength is the clear timeline of your exit, while your weakness is the lack of written proof gathered so far, such as payslips and your employment agreement. You can formally claim unpaid wages before the government-appointed authority within 3 years [KB:cow_s45].

options.title: Send a formal written demand email
options.what_to_do: Write an email to HR and management demanding your pending full and final settlement of Rs 110,000 immediately, citing that delayed payments cause financial loss.

options.title: File a complaint with the Labour Department
options.what_to_do: If HR does not respond or refuses to pay, approach the local Labour Commissioner office in Gurgaon to file a formal claim for unpaid wages.

proof_tips: Send a WhatsApp message or email to HR asking them to confirm the exact calculated full and final amount in writing.
Download your bank statements showing the credit of your previous monthly salaries from the company.
Request your relieving letter and official F&F statement via email if you haven't received them yet.
what_i_dont_know: Whether your signed employment contract explicitly includes a valid 90-day F&F clause agreed upon by you
Exact breakup of the Rs 110,000 pending amount into salary, leave encashment, or other components
assessment.needs_lawyer_reason: A lawyer is not needed at this initial stage since you can first send a written demand or approach the Labour Department yourself. A lawyer would only be necessary if the company initiates legal proceedings against you or refuses completely after a formal labour complaint.
assessment.reply: You have a strong legal basis to claim your pending full and final settlement of Rs 110,000. Although HR is citing a 90-day company policy, the law requires wages to be paid within two working days of resignation [KB:src_cow_2019_17]. Your first step is to send a formal written email to HR demanding your dues and pointing out this delay. If they still fail to pay, you can approach the Labour Department in Gurgaon to file a formal claim within 3 years [KB:cow_s45]. Do you currently have a copy of your employment agreement or company policy stating the 90-day F&F clause?
